vibe.rationale: Vibe 4 — consistent with July 12 morning but with the strongest upward pressure since the July 11 brief. Two overnight positive reversals define the morning brief's tone. First and most significant: the B and O Fire achieved 19% containment overnight despite the most challenging suppression conditions of its arc — Red Flag Warning, strong winds, east Cascades onset terrain at Day 16. The July 12 morning brief characterized the fire at 0% containment, Level 3 evacuations, under expected Red Flag — the worst-case suppression configuration. Overnight, suppression crews established containment lines that survived those conditions. The perimeter held at 2,927 acres. Level 3 (Go Now) evacuations for Okanogan County have been downgraded to Level 2 — a structural step down from the most urgent evacuation category. Strike teams have been sent to reinforce. The 19% containment under Red Flag is operationally decisive: it demonstrates that the fire is controllable under adverse conditions, not in the Kartar rapid-escalation pattern the July 12 brief flagged as the primary risk. This positive development alone would justify holding at Vibe 4 rather than dropping to Vibe 3. Second: the measles June 19 Lumen Field primary incubation window appears resolved. July 12 was Day 10, the sub-window's final day. The three-day consecutive clean streak through Days 8-9-10 (July 10-11-12) — the highest secondary-transmission-chain identification probability window — is the best epidemiological sequence possible for this arc. Georgetown University wastewater DNA close confirmation is expected, at which point the brief will characterize the June 19 cluster risk as resolved for the primary window. Third positive: Chelan Hills Fire (Day 9) is expected to reach 100% containment today. If confirmed, it marks the completion of the July 4-13 emergency response arc for the 2026 Washington fire season's most consequential WUI event. Dominant negative 1: WTI above $74 (+4% Monday open) as markets price the Iran Gulf Arab state ballistic missile attacks (5 nations targeted Saturday night — Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, Oman, Qatar — all intercepted), the IRGC Hormuz closure declaration, and the Ghalibaf MOU-violation accusation from Iran's parliamentary leadership. The WTI +4% move on Monday open means Warsh's September FOMC deflationary thesis — premised on energy price deceleration — is under acute challenge at the start of the week. Dominant negative 2: Qatar diplomatic channel survival unknown. Qatar — host of the June 19 MOU communication architecture — was targeted with Iranian ballistic missiles Saturday night. Channel status unconfirmed as of Monday morning. Dominant negative 3: first US Ebola case (Bundibugyo strain, US humanitarian worker, DRC, July 11) adds a new domestic public health thread at the moment the measles sub-window is resolving. Drop to Vibe 3 requires: fourth US-Iran kinetic exchange Monday July 13 with no diplomatic output; WTI spiking above $76; Qatar communication channel formally suspended; B and O Fire re-escalation above 5,000 acres under ongoing east-wind onset conditions; US Ebola transmission beyond index case confirmed. Upgrade to Vibe 5 requires: Chelan Hills confirmed 100% contained with all evacuations lifted; Georgetown July 12 measles close confirmed clean; WTI declining below $72; Qatar diplomatic channel confirmed operative after overnight targeting; June CPI confirms at or below 3.8%.

items.summary: The July 13 morning brief opens on Hormuz MOU Acute Stress Day 6 without a confirmed fourth US-Iran kinetic exchange overnight into Monday. The third exchange — Saturday night July 11-12, US response to Iran's Cyprus-flagged container ship attack (1 crew member missing) — remains the last confirmed kinetic event. The three MOU termination-instrument absences that define the MOU's legal operative status continue to hold: no SNSC formal void declaration, no CENTCOM naval blockade reinstatement, no Kharg Island strike. The MOU is under acute stress on Day 25 but has not been formally terminated. The Monday morning WTI re-escalation above $74 (+4%) is the markets' delayed reaction to the Saturday night sequence: the Iran Gulf Arab state attacks (ballistic missiles and drones targeting Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, Oman, and Qatar — all intercepted), the IRGC's Hormuz closure declaration (countered by CENTCOM), and Iran Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf's formal MOU-violation accusation from Tehran's legislative leadership. The Monday WTI +4% move means the July 11 normalization signal (sub-$72 WTI) has been fully unwound and the energy component driver of Warsh's September FOMC deflationary thesis is under acute challenge at the start of the week. The Qatar diplomatic channel remains the morning's single highest-priority analytical unknown. The channel — confirmed operative July 11 daytime per Al Arabiya/Times of Israel — is hosted by a nation that was targeted with Iranian ballistic missiles that same Saturday night. Whether the Doha architecture survived Iran targeting Qatar with ballistic missiles is unconfirmed as of Monday morning. The 24 hours since the exchange without a confirmed fourth kinetic event is the minimal-positive: the absence of a fourth exchange overnight is consistent with either a managed diplomatic pause or the logistical tempo of US strike planning cycles. The brief cannot assign probability to either interpretation without confirmed channel output. Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei remains in hiding — in place since the Israeli February 28 assassination of his father — communicating only through written statements without public face or voice. Every Iranian negotiating signal carries the structural ambiguity of a principal-level communications architecture operating through couriers. June CPI releases tomorrow (July 14, 8:30 AM ET). Cleveland Fed nowcast: approximately 3.8% year-over-year, down from 4.2% in May. Kiplinger analysis notes the headline could flip negative on energy price base effects — a potentially misleading headline that would not reflect underlying core pressures. NY Fed June consumer survey shows one-year inflation expectations at 3.7%, the highest since September 2023. June CPI is the most consequential single data release for the brief's economic arc since the May CPI on June 10.

items.summary: Six secondary geopolitical threads on July 13 morning. First: FIFA World Cup 2026 semifinals are confirmed. France vs. Spain plays Tuesday July 14 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. England vs. Argentina plays Wednesday July 15. Argentina advanced on Julian Alvarez's 112th-minute long-range strike against Switzerland. The dual semifinal window (July 14-15) coincides with the June CPI release (July 14) and the Peru JNE credentials ceremony (July 15) — a dense geopolitical-economic convergence window. Both semifinal venues carry NIFC-FIFA mass venue co-response posture under PL4 Day 15. Second: Russia fuel crisis Day 13. Omsk refinery remains 75% offline — CDU-10 destroyed (multi-month restoration), CDU-11 offline (infrastructure damage, multi-month). Russia's diesel export ban through end of July sustains Central Asian spillover: Uzbekistan flight cuts active; Kazakhstan Chinese import-insurance continuing. IEA 'unprecedented' dual-shock designation stands. The overnight Iran Gulf escalation reinforces the dual two-source energy shock as the dominant inflationary macro backdrop. Warsh's September FOMC deflationary thesis now requires three concurrent favorable conditions — Hormuz normalization, Russian refining recovery, and commodity price relief — none of which are in progress. Third: Lebanon fragile hold Day 28. The 48-hour post-third-exchange window opened July 11 and closes through Monday July 13 morning. No confirmed Hezbollah mobilization orders through overnight. The Iran Gulf Arab state attacks Saturday night — Iran demonstrating willingness to escalate horizontally across five nations — increased the analytic uncertainty about Hezbollah mobilization sanctioning. Clean through Monday morning morning is cautiously positive but the Lebanon assessment remains at heightened monitoring posture. Fourth: Ebola DRC/Uganda PHEIC Day 58 — new significant development. The 2026 Ebola epidemic was declared a WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 16. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus (distinct from the Zaire strain for which existing treatments are certified) has now spread to four DRC provinces: Ituri (epicenter, 1,631 cases / 535 deaths / 25 of 36 health zones), North Kivu (158 cases / 89 deaths), South Kivu (3 cases / 1 death), and Haut-Uélé (spread confirmed June 29). Total deaths as of early July: approximately 702 DRC + 2 Uganda. WHO reports the outbreak is 'spreading largely undetected.' The most acute new development: on July 11, the United States confirmed that a US citizen humanitarian worker testing positive for Ebola while working in DRC — the first confirmed US case in the 2026 arc. This adds Ebola to the domestic public health monitoring stack at the moment the measles primary window is resolving. France confirmed an imported case June 24. Fifth: Peru JNE credentials ceremony T-2 (July 15, Gran Teatro Nacional San Borja, noon). Keiko Fujimori (won by 49,641 votes in full official count, June 30; JNE declared president-elect July 3) and VPs Galarreta and Torres credential ceremony tomorrow. Argentine President Milei attendance confirmed. Inauguration July 28. No transition complications. Sixth: Colombia T-25 to de la Espriella inauguration August 7. Seventh: Venezuela earthquake Day 20 — 1,719+ confirmed dead, 46,600+ missing. Maduro continuing to restrict US humanitarian access.

items.summary: The July 13 morning economic session opens with WTI re-escalating above $74 — a +4% Monday open as markets price the Saturday night sequence: Iran's Gulf Arab state ballistic missile attacks (five nations targeted, all intercepted), the IRGC's Hormuz closure declaration, and the Ghalibaf MOU-violation accusation. The sub-$72 WTI normalization signal from July 11 has been fully unwound. The +4% Monday move adds a new pricing layer on top of the war-risk premium already building from the third US-Iran exchange and the Cyprus-flag crew casualty (1 missing confirmed). The Gulf Arab state targeting introduced a commercial infrastructure risk dimension distinct from the Hormuz corridor war-risk premium: Bahrain hosts the US Fifth Fleet (Hormuz operations center), UAE hosts major bunkering and logistics hubs, Qatar hosts Al Udeid Air Base and the diplomatic communication channel, Jordan and Oman host US military personnel and basing infrastructure. The IRGC closure declaration — countered operationally by CENTCOM ('Strait is open') — creates routing uncertainty for tanker operators regardless of whether CENTCOM can enforce the counter-declaration. Lloyd's war-risk normalization window is analytically suspended. June CPI releases tomorrow (July 14, 8:30 AM ET). Cleveland Fed nowcast: 3.8% year-over-year, down from 4.2% in May. Kiplinger analysis notes the headline could flip negative due to energy price base effects from the oil price declines between April and June — a potentially misleading negative headline that would not reflect underlying core pressures from tariffs, shelter costs, and food prices. The more operative signal is core CPI and whether it continues the deceleration trend. NY Fed June consumer survey showed one-year-ahead inflation expectations at 3.7% — the highest since September 2023 — indicating that household forward inflation pricing is moving in the wrong direction for Warsh's September FOMC thesis. Kevin Warsh's hawkish hold framework (September rate hike 61% CME FedWatch; June SEP median of 1-2 hikes in 2026; core PCE year-end forecast 3.4%) is premised on energy price deceleration through late summer. The July 13 Monday WTI +4% move above $74 is the most direct challenge to that thesis since the July 7 re-escalation began. For Warsh's September FOMC scenario to proceed on the deflationary path, three conditions must materialize simultaneously: (1) Hormuz war-risk premium normalization (WTI sustained below $72), (2) Russian refinery crisis resolution (multi-month timeline — not in progress), and (3) commodity price relief from tariff moderation. None of the three conditions are moving in the favorable direction as of July 13 morning. Tariff calendar: Section 122 expires July 24 (T-11); USTR Section 301 completion deadline July 20 (T-7). The 3-4 day July 20-24 gap between Section 301 completion and Section 122 expiry remains the operative importer planning concern. No White House Section 301 successor structure announced. Pharma 232 July 31 (T-18). FERC AI 30-day report July 18 (T-5 — final week).

items.summary: Three secondary economic threads this morning. First: OBBB Law Day 14 (signed June 29, effective July 1). Medicaid work requirements and SNAP restrictions now active in 18 states. The most significant legal development since the July 12 brief: on June 22, 2026, a federal district court issued a ruling in Aragon v. Rollins holding that the USDA exceeded its legal authority when it approved state demonstration projects restricting what SNAP participants could purchase. The ruling invalidates USDA approvals of SNAP food-restriction demonstrations in Colorado, Iowa, Nebraska, Tennessee, and West Virginia. This is the Aragon v. Rollins downstream exposure the July 12 brief identified; the June 22 ruling is now operative precedent. Note that SNAP food-restriction effective date under OBBB is July 31 — the Aragon v. Rollins ruling creates a collision between the OBBB's statutory mandate and the federal court's USDA authority limitation. Zero federal stays on Medicaid work requirement titles through morning. CBO 10-year deficit estimate ($3.4T) remains the operative fiscal impact assessment. Second: Russia CDU-11 continues offline at Day 13. The combined 75% Omsk offline picture is unchanged — multi-month structural story. The Monday WTI +4% means both components of the dual energy shock constraining Warsh's September SEP thesis are active simultaneously: Hormuz war-risk re-escalating and Russian refining on multi-month recovery. Third: World Cup 2026 economic co-response window. Semifinal at AT&T Stadium Arlington TX (France vs Spain, July 14) and second semifinal (July 15) create a July 14-15 dense convergence window: June CPI release (July 14 morning), Peru JNE credentials (July 15 noon), and two World Cup semifinal events. Dallas-Fort Worth hospitality sector response at maximum capacity; NIFC-FIFA venue co-response framework active for both semifinal sites.

items.summary: The July 13 morning infrastructure session is defined by the overnight positive reversal of the B and O Fire — the most significant single PNW fire suppression development since the Chelan Hills 95% containment breakthrough on July 11. The B and O Fire (near Okanogan, Okanogan County WA, ignition July 9, human-caused/under investigation) achieved 19% containment overnight despite Red Flag Warning conditions and strong winds that constituted the most challenging suppression environment of the fire's arc. The perimeter held at 2,927 acres. Level 3 (Go Now) evacuations for Okanogan County areas have been downgraded to Level 2 — a structural step down from the acute-emergency characterization the July 12 brief carried at open (Level 3, 0% containment, 2,000+ acres). Strike teams have been dispatched to reinforce the 359 personnel and 19 engines, 3 hand crews, and 3 helicopters already assigned. The 19% containment under Red Flag conditions is operationally decisive: it means suppression crews established firelines that survived the most adverse weather conditions the fire is likely to encounter during the onset period. The Kartar rapid-escalation risk pattern the July 12 brief identified as the primary B and O analog — rapid overnight escalation to large-fire scale with catastrophic WUI potential — has not actuated. The fire remains in the east Cascades onset region (Day 16) under 4th-year drought fuel conditions, and additional Red Flag periods are possible, but the perimeter holding through the first Red Flag event is the dominant suppression reassurance signal of the morning. The July 12 morning brief's characterization of the B and O Fire as the 'highest-consequence unresolved PNW fire' is updated to 'stabilizing under active suppression with initial containment lines established.' Chelan Hills Fire (Day 9, Douglas County WA): full containment expected today as mop-up and patrol operations mature following the 95% Day 8 breakthrough. Douglas County officials have issued a $25,000 reward to identify the person responsible for the human-caused ignition. All evacuations are expected to be lifted upon 100% containment confirmation. Final acreage: 9,861. Structures destroyed: 19 primary residences + 6 damaged. Preliminary damage: $9.1M+. Fatality: 1. The McNeil Canyon recovery phase (utility restoration, insurance representatives, access caution advisories) begins upon 100% confirmation. Sourdough Fire (Day 9, North Cascades NP, Whatcom County): SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) confirmed open. Skagit dam hydropower (Gorge, Diablo, Ross) continuing partial recovery under Seattle City Light. Extended attack managed posture without new WUI or SR-20 threat. NIFC Preparedness Level 4 Day 15 (first PL4 since 2021): 38+ large fires nationally burning 541,000+ acres across 14+ states. Washington State YTD: 705 wildfires burning 117,000+ acres as of mid-July — on pace for one of the most active seasons on record.

items.summary: Five secondary infrastructure threads this morning. First: PNW Climate Week opens today (July 13-19, 2026 — first cross-region climate week in North America, spanning Seattle, Vancouver BC, and Portland). The forum's Day 1 agenda covers AI Data Centers, Energy, and Communities; WA State Climate Policy (Rep. Jayapal and Microsoft CSO Melanie Nakagawa featured); and energy infrastructure and carbon removal. The B and O Fire's overnight positive reversal (19% containment, Level 2) provides a cautiously improved fire backdrop for Day 1 compared to the worst-case scenario the July 12 brief projected. But the forum still opens with Washington State at 705 fires / 117,000+ acres YTD, NIFC PL4 Day 15, Chelan Hills WUI catastrophe in fresh recovery, and 4th-year drought — the most operationally acute fire and drought context in the forum's history. FERC AI T-5 (July 18) means Days 1-5 of PNW Climate Week directly precede and inform the six ISO/RTO submissions for the FERC AI large-load integration 30-day informational report — the most consequential national energy governance timeline converging with the forum. Day 1 outputs that address AI data center electricity demand governance for the Quincy WA/The Dalles OR corridors are materially consequential for FERC's July 18 deadline regulatory context. Second: FERC show-cause orders to all six ISO/RTOs on large energy user grid connection tariff justification (60-day response deadline: August 17). FERC's parallel elimination of cumulative NEPA environmental effects analysis as a standard project review component continues to streamline large-load integration approval pathways. Third: DOE Energy Dominance Financing office $17.5 billion conditional loan commitment for nuclear reactor component procurement — largest single federal nuclear investment in decades (four companies: Titan Mining/Anniston AL graphite, EnergyX/Pine Bluff AR lithium, Ioneer/Red River TX boron, REalloys/Tooele UT heavy rare earths at Army depot leases). The Hormuz re-escalation context: the nuclear/critical minerals commitment is a long-cycle supply diversification instrument at a moment when the near-term energy shock is re-escalating Monday morning. Fourth: Longview CSB Day 49 — Elevated Risk Window Day 3. No chemical incident through overnight. Summer heat at lower Columbia River corridor persisting post-atmospheric river. Nippon Dynawave active monitoring. The CSB elevated window runs through July 18 (concurrent with FERC AI T-5 and PNW Climate Week Days 1-5). Fifth: Washington drought emergency Day 39. Fourth consecutive year; 50% snowpack; 12-county emergency; 705 wildfires / 117,000+ acres YTD. Federal forecasters: Columbia River Basin is the most likely spot in the West to see drought intensify over the next three months. El Nino at 61% probability; Super El Nino at 25%. NSF Newport OR ocean observatory Dark Day 15 — 5+ major weather/fire events have now occurred without the coastal atmospheric monitoring anchor. Senate unanimous reinstallation authorization in place; physical reinstallation timeline pending.
